India’s Aerospace Story Is Taking Off, Literally. ✈️🇮🇳

For a long time, India’s aerospace story was largely about buying aircraft and flying in them.

Now, there’s another story taking shape: building the aircraft ecosystem behind them.

Indian companies are increasingly becoming part of global aerospace supply chains, manufacturing aerostructures, precision components, assemblies, forgings and other highly engineered parts.

And that shift is important.

Because the real question is no longer:
“How many aircraft will India buy?”

It is increasingly:
“How much of the aircraft can India help build?”

From Tata and Mahindra to Dynamatic, Aequs, Bharat Forge, MTAR and several emerging players, Indian manufacturing is finding its place in some of the world’s most demanding aerospace programmes.

The next challenge is to move beyond being the “good-value supplier” and become the “go-to engineering partner.”

In aerospace, even a tiny component has to survive thousands of hours in the sky.

So yes, the margins may be measured in millimetres, but the opportunity for India is measured in billions.

The Indian aerospace story is no longer just about flying higher.

It is about building higher up the value chain.

And that, perhaps, is the most exciting part. 🚀
